note: Study 02 (GitLab work data). Written before pulling.

hypotheses.statement: Waiting for the first review is a large part of how long a change takes, for every role.
hypotheses.disproved_if: Median time to first review is under 10% of median time to merge, for merged MRs in the sample, in all three projects.

hypotheses.statement: Non-engineers' changes wait longer than engineers' changes of a similar size in the same project (the Blast Radius claim, measured).
hypotheses.disproved_if: In the handbook and marketing-site projects, the median time to first review for MRs by non-engineers (design, product, marketing, other) is no more than 1.25x that of engineers, comparing MRs that change 3 files or fewer.

hypotheses.statement: Changes that need reviewers from more than one role take clearly longer than changes reviewed by a single role (approval chains slow work).
hypotheses.disproved_if: Median time to merge for merged MRs whose reviewers span two or more roles is no more than 1.25x that of MRs reviewed within one role, in gitlab-org/gitlab.
